vt26_gospel_of_mary.topic: Gospel of Mary: manuscripts, outline, teachings, Peter/Andrew vs Mary, Levi; Gregory I homily 33 (c.591); 1969 calendar; 2016 feast; women's ordination teaching

claims.text: Berlin Codex (P. Berol. 8502, Akhmim Codex): bought by Carl Reinhardt in Cairo, January 1896; reportedly found wrapped in feathers in a wall niche at a Christian burial site (Akhmim); Sahidic Coptic papyrus, early 5th c. (possibly late 4th); contains Gospel of Mary (pp.1-6, 11-14 missing), Apocryphon of John, Sophia of Jesus Christ, Act of Peter; Schmidt presented it 16 July 1896; Till's edition of gnostic texts 1955; held in Berlin

Greek fragments P.Ryl. 463 (published 1938) and P.Oxy. 3525 (published 1983), 3rd c.; less than half of the text survives; King dates composition early 2nd c., Tuckett first half of 2nd c.; Decretum Gelasianum's list does not name it

Outline: lost opening; Saviour on matter and sin (7,1-9,4); disciples grieve, Mary comforts them (9,5-20); Mary's vision and soul's ascent past powers (9,20-17,7); Andrew and Peter challenge, Levi defends (17,7-19,2)

Mattison translation: 'Sin doesn't exist, but you're the ones who make sin' (p.7); 'the Son of Humanity exists within you' (p.8); 'Don't lay down any rules beyond what I've given you, nor make a law like the lawgiver, lest you be bound by it' (p.9); 'where the mind is, there is the treasure' (p.10); fourth power with seven forms; Peter: 'He didn't speak with a woman without our knowledge...?'; Andrew: 'I myself don't believe that the Savior said these things'; Levi: 'if the Savior made her worthy, who are you then to reject her?'; ending: they went out to teach and preach
Which Mary: most scholars Magdalene (King); Shoemaker and Jones propose mother of Jesus; King reads the conflict as 2nd-c. tension over esoteric revelation and women's teaching authority
Gregory I Homily 33 (Rome, c.591): identified Luke's sinner, Mary of Bethany and Mary Magdalene; 'what are these seven demons, if not the universality of all vices?'; does not use word prostitute

Canonical gospels: Magdalene at empty tomb in all four (Mark 16:1, Matt 28:1, Luke 24:1, John 20:1), first to see risen Jesus in John 20; named at crucifixion in Mark, Matthew, John; 1969 calendar revision made 22 July memorial refer to Magdalene only, separating Mary of Bethany; Eastern Orthodox view her as 'Equal to the Apostles'

Decree of Congregation for Divine Worship dated 3 June 2016, by express wish of Pope Francis, raised Mary Magdalene's memorial to a feast; Roche cites Rabanus Maurus and Thomas Aquinas for 'apostolorum apostola'; notes Western tradition after Gregory conflated her
Epiphanius, Panarion 26.8, names a 'Greater Questions of Mary' (and a 'Lesser') used by group he calls Borborites, alleging an obscene revelation; text does not survive
Ordinatio Sacerdotalis 22 May 1994: 'the Church has no authority whatsoever to confer priestly ordination on women' and 'this judgment is to be definitively held'; cites 'the twelve men'
Petrocchi commission report released 4 Dec 2025 at Leo XIV's request: rules out women deacons as a degree of Holy Orders (2022 vote 7-1) but says judgment not definitive

vt26_gospel_of_judas.topic: Gospel of Judas: Irenaeus c.180, Epiphanius; Codex Tchacos provenance; NatGeo 2006; outline; DeConick dispute; Benedict XVI 2006

claims.text: Irenaeus AH I.31.1 (c.180): a group says Judas 'alone, knowing the truth as no others did, accomplished the mystery of the betrayal' and they produce 'a fictitious history... which they style the Gospel of Judas'; identity with Tchacos text uncertain
Epiphanius's Panarion (begun 374/375, issued c.3 years later) attacks 'Cainites' who used a Gospel of Judas

Codex Tchacos: found 1970s near Maghagha/El Minya; sold 1978 to Cairo dealer Hanna; stolen to Geneva c.1980, recovered 1982; Emmel examined 1983 ($3m asked); Hicksville NY safe-deposit box c.1984-2000; Nussberger-Tchacos bought April 2000; Yale declined; Ferrini froze it; Maecenas Foundation Feb 2001; Kasser announced July 2004; radiocarbon 220-340 CE; ~1,000 fragments; 90-95% restored; NatGeo unveiled translation 6 April 2006; critical edition 2007; pages to go to Coptic Museum Cairo
Codex contents: Letter of Peter to Philip, First Apocalypse of James, Gospel of Judas, fragment of Book/Temptation of Allogenes

Outline/quotes (Kasser, Meyer, Wurst 2006 trans.): 'The secret account of the revelation that Jesus spoke in conversation with Judas Iscariot'; Jesus laughs at disciples' eucharist; Judas: 'You are from the immortal realm of Barbelo'; temple vision, 'the cattle you have seen brought for sacrifice are the many people you lead astray'; cosmology of luminous cloud, Nebro/Yaldabaoth, Saklas; 'you will sacrifice the man that clothes me'; thirteenth; Judas enters cloud; hands Jesus over for money

DeConick, NYT 1 Dec 2007 and The Thirteenth Apostle (2007): daimon = demon; Judas separated 'from' the holy generation; dropped negation - will not ascend; NatGeo said virtually all issues addressed in footnotes; Pagels on 'handing over'; Rowan Williams 2006 'demonstrably late text'; Gagné on apophasis

Benedict XVI Holy Thursday 13 April 2006: Judas 'evaluated Jesus in accordance with the criteria of power and success'; 'obscure mystery of rejection'; no mention of the Gospel of Judas. General Audience 18 Oct 2006: 'it is not up to us to judge his gesture'; Gospels point to Satan's influence and Judas's responsibility
Jan 2006 Times of London reported Vatican scholars (Brandmüller quoted) would give Judas a 'makeover'; no Vatican act followed

Pagels (with King, Reading Judas, 2007): the gospel is 'a kind of protest literature' against church leaders whom the author saw as encouraging believers to die for God; questions whether God requires a son's death; Judas's act was 'obedience to a command or request'

vt26_pistis_sophia.topic: Pistis Sophia: Askew Codex, content, Sophia's repentances, Mary and Peter, renunciations, Books of Jeu (Bruce Codex), Mead

claims.text: Askew Codex: bought by Anthony Askew 1772 from a bookseller; British Museum bought from heirs 1785; BL Add MS 5114; parchment, 178 leaves (356 pp), pp.337-344 missing; two scribes; provenance unknown, most probably Egypt; Schwartze Coptic + Latin publ. posthumously by Petermann 1851; Schmidt German 1905; Mead English 1896, rev. 1921

Composition probably 3rd-4th c.; manuscript late 4th c. per some; four books, Book 4 likely separate/earlier; Jesus 11 years (ch.1; some count 12) with disciples after resurrection; Sophia in thirteenth aeon, deceived, descends into chaos, repentances interpreted by disciples via Psalms and Odes of Solomon; Mary Magdalene most prominent questioner; Schmidt/Harnack attributed to Ophites; crucifixion not described

Mead ch.1: 'when Jesus had risen from the dead, that he passed eleven years discoursing with his disciples'; ch.31: Sophia mistakes the lion-faced power of 'the triple-powered Self-willed', leaves 'the thirteenth æon'; ch.57 thirteenth repentance interpreted by Martha; ch.36 Peter: 'we will not endure this woman, for she taketh the opportunity from us'; ch.72 Mary: 'I am afraid of Peter, because he threatened me and hateth our sex', answer: 'Every one who shall be filled with the spirit of light to come forward... no one shall be able to prevent him'; ch.102 'Renounce the whole world...' with list incl. slander, false witness, avarice, wrath, adultery, murder, magic potions, doctrines of error

Bruce Codex: bought by James Bruce c.1769 in Upper Egypt near Medinet Habu; Bodleian 'Bruce 96' since 1848; Books of Jeu and Untitled Text; Schmidt 1892; MacDermot 1978; very poor condition; Pistis Sophia refers to Books of Jeu (ch.99, 134)
Mead: Theosophist from 1884, Blavatsky's secretary 1889, founded Quest Society 1909; helped popularise 'Gnosis'; Quispel suggested he influenced Jung
